title: Lake Vornholm
text: Lake Vornholm is a freshwater lake in the province of Easthaven. It covers an area of 42 square kilometres and has a maximum depth of 87 metres. The lake was formed by glacial activity about 12,000 years ago. The town of Marrow Bay lies on its northern shore. The lake is home to a large population of brown trout and is a popular destination for sailing and kayaking. The Vorn River flows out of the lake at its southern end and joins the sea near the port of Kellmouth.

title: Tessa Quillfeather
text: Tessa Quillfeather (born 3 May 1961) is a marine biologist from Northport. She studied biology at the University of Northport and completed her doctorate in 1989. Quillfeather is known for her research on deep-sea coral reefs in the Ardent Trench. In 2004 she received the Harwick Medal for her work on coral conservation. She led the Northport Ocean Institute from 2008 to 2019 and has written three books, including The Quiet Reef (2012).

title: Brindle Engine
text: The Brindle Engine is a two-stroke steam engine designed by the engineer Oswin Brindle in 1874. It was first used to power textile mills in the town of Carrowfield. The engine was notable for its compact double-cylinder design, which reduced coal consumption by about a third compared with earlier engines. Production ended in 1902, and a restored example is displayed at the Carrowfield Museum of Industry.
